headline: Egypt parliament APPROVES authorising President El-Sisi to send military support to defend Saudi Arabia if Riyadh requests it
dek: Egypt's parliament authorised President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi to take the necessary measures to support/defend Saudi Arabia, if Riyadh requests help against Ansar Allah attacks. Authorisation does NOT mean immediate deployment: El-Sisi has said Egypt acts only if asked, and on Oct 21 limited the scope…
sources: Reuters (parliamentarians + local media); Al-Ahram state newspaper via Arab News; MP Mostafa Bakry on X via The National
fault_line: Arab solidarity vs hypocrisy: Egypt arms itself for Saudi Arabia while Gaza burns — supporters cite constitutional process and national pride, detractors call it mercenary politics (social threads polarised, profanity-he

sections.what_happened: Egypt's parliament authorised President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi to take the necessary measures to support/defend Saudi Arabia, if Riyadh requests help against Ansar Allah attacks. Authorisation does NOT mean immediate deployment: El-Sisi has said Egypt acts only if asked, and on Oct 21 limited the scope to defending Saudi territory/borders, not attacking Yemen. Under Article 152, a foreign combat mission needs two-thirds of the 596-member house (398 MPs); the vote was held by roll call behind closed doors and the tally was not published.
sections.what_verified: Reuters original (parliamentarians + local media) + The National (MP Bakry X post, closed session, third session in nine days) + Arab News (Al-Ahram: House 'approved authorizing President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi to take the necessary measures to support the Kingdom') + Jerusalem Post Reuters carry. Vote tally unpublished, so the margin is NOT confirmed.
sections.what_disputed: No Saudi request has been announced (Reuters/The National agree); Sisi's Oct 21 defensive-only limit contradicts any reading of this as an offensive Yemen deployment authorisation. Egypt has not joined the August Mecca mutual-defence pact (Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Türkiye); FM Abdelatty: membership 'under serious consideration'. No deployment, force size or duration specified by the National Defence Council.
sections.why_matters: Egypt just cleared the last legal hurdle to enter the Gulf war — but no Saudi request, no troops yet. The vote that took 9 days and ~500 MPs wanting to speak.
